about: "Allow this from now on", its second half (docs/allow-from-now-on.md): before a phone signs KIFF's draft, every key on each of the draft's Cards is one the apps' check reads. `keys` lists them by object. A key whose value is null sets nothing and passes. On a Card, `id` must be the Card it revises. A `quantity_of` must say what its `quantity` says: "sum(amount_cents)" is {kind: sum, parameter: amount_cents}, and "count" is {kind: count}. Anything else is not what was offered, and nothing is signed. Each case sets JSON pointers (RFC 6901) on contracts/kiff-agent-draft-from-hold.json, KIFF's own answer, then says whether the keys pass. Keys of the draft itself (its id, version, widens…) aren't a Card's and aren't checked here.

read_not_compared.lines: KIFF's words for the Card, shown to the person: never a term
read_not_compared.title: a grant's words, shown: never a term
read_not_compared.current.active: the Card in force is live: a draft revises only a live Card
read_not_compared.current.domain_id: the Card in force's domain, as KIFF stores it beside `domain`, which is compared
read_not_compared.current.hold_expiry_seconds: how long a held call waits under the Card in force; a draft that sets `hold_expiry` is refused, so it stays
